# Aster

> Aster is a free natal (birth) chart generator that runs entirely in the browser. Give it a birth date, local time and place, and it draws a chart wheel with planet positions, houses and aspects. Calculations use the Swiss Ephemeris compiled to WebAssembly; nothing entered is sent to a server unless the visitor chooses to send it.

Aster is a single page at https://aster.myles.garden/. The page has no server-side rendering: the chart is calculated and drawn by JavaScript in the visitor's browser. A tool that fetches the page without running JavaScript will see only the empty form, not a chart. Use the JSON API below instead. Once opened in a browser, the page also works offline: a service worker caches it and the calculation engine.

## JSON API

A small JSON API runs on a server and calculates the same charts, with the same Swiss Ephemeris engine. Prefer it to scraping the page. The OpenAPI document, with every field described, is at https://aster.myles.garden/api/v1/openapi.json.

```
POST /api/v1/chart
POST /api/v1/transits
POST /api/v1/progressions
POST /api/v1/solar-return
POST /api/v1/lunar-return
POST /api/v1/synastry
POST /api/v1/composite
GET  /api/v1/places?q=
```

`POST /api/v1/chart` takes a JSON body:

```json
{
  "date": "1990-05-15",
  "time": "14:30",
  "latitude": 43.7064,
  "longitude": -79.3986,
  "timeZone": "America/Toronto",
  "houseSystem": "placidus"
}
```

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | Yes | `YYYY-MM-DD`. Roughly 3000 BCE to 3000 CE. |
| `time` | No | Local clock time at the birthplace, `HH:MM`, 24-hour. Do not convert to UTC. Leave it out when the birth time isn't known. |
| `latitude`, `longitude` | Yes | Decimal degrees, south and west negative. |
| `timeZone` | Yes | IANA time zone of the birthplace. Aster applies its historical offset, daylight saving included. |
| `houseSystem` | No | One of `placidus`, `koch`, `wholeSign`, `equal`, `porphyry`, `regiomontanus` or `campanus`. Defaults to `placidus`. |
| `aspectSet` | No | `major` for conjunctions, sextiles, squares, trines and oppositions, or `all` to add semi-sextiles, semi-squares, sesquiquadrates and quincunxes. Defaults to `major`. |
| `orbSize` | No | `tight` (three quarters of standard), `standard` or `wide` (a quarter more). Defaults to `standard`. |
| `ayanamsa` | No | For the sidereal zodiac: `lahiri`, `faganBradley`, `krishnamurti`, `raman`, `yukteshwar` or `trueChitra`. Leave it out for the tropical zodiac. |
| `placeName` | No | A name for the place, shown when the share link is opened. |

It returns the birth moment in UTC, each body's longitude, sign, degree within the sign, retrograde status and house, the 12 house cusps with the ascendant and midheaven, the aspects between planets, each with its `rank` (`major` or `minor`), and a `shareUrl` that draws the same chart on the site. A sidereal chart also returns its `ayanamsa` and `ayanamsaDegrees`, how far behind the tropical zodiac it is; every longitude is already moved back by that. Without a `time`, houses and angles are left out and each body lists the signs it may be in. Inside the polar circles, Placidus and Koch houses can't be calculated, so the houses are cast as Porphyry: `effectiveHouseSystem` names the system actually used, and `houseSystem` the one asked for. Invalid input is answered with HTTP 400 and `{ "error": "..." }`.

`POST /api/v1/transits` sets the sky at a moment against a natal chart. Its body nests the chart's request whole, as `natal`, with an optional `at`:

```json
{
  "natal": {
    "date": "1990-05-15",
    "time": "14:30",
    "latitude": 43.7064,
    "longitude": -79.3986,
    "timeZone": "America/Toronto"
  },
  "at": "2026-11-18T10:00:00-05:00"
}
```

`at` is an ISO 8601 date and time with a UTC offset or `Z`, to the minute; leave it out for now. It returns the natal chart, the bodies at `at`, each with the natal house it's crossing, and the aspects they make to the natal bodies within 2°. Each aspect's `first` body is natal and its `second` is transiting, and its `timing` gives when it comes into orb (`entersOrb`), every moment it's exact (`exact`, up to three as a planet turns retrograde) and when it leaves orb (`leavesOrb`), searched up to five years either way. The `shareUrl` draws the transits on the site. Positions follow the natal chart's zodiac.

`POST /api/v1/progressions` moves a natal chart on a day for each year of life. It takes `natal` and an optional `date`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, from the birth date on, defaulting to today in UTC. It returns the progressed bodies, each with the natal house it's in, and their aspects to the natal bodies within 1°, natal body `first`.

`POST /api/v1/solar-return` finds the chart for the moment the Sun gets back to its natal position. It takes `natal`, which needs a `time`, an optional `year` after the year of birth, defaulting to the return in effect now, and an optional `place`, `{ latitude, longitude, timeZone, placeName }`, defaulting to the birthplace. `POST /api/v1/lunar-return` does the same for the Moon, about every 27 days, with an optional `date` in place of `year`: it finds the latest return by the end of that date where it's cast, defaulting to today there. Both return the natal chart and the return's `chart`, whose `bornAt` is the moment of the return, to the second.

`POST /api/v1/synastry` compares two people's charts. It takes `first`, a full chart request, and `second`, only `date`, `time`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `timeZone` and `placeName`: the second chart uses the first's house system, aspect settings and zodiac. It returns both charts, the aspects between them, first person's body `first`, and which of each person's houses the other's bodies fall in. `POST /api/v1/composite` takes the same body and returns one chart made from the midpoints of the two, with houses only when both birth times are known.

Every chart endpoint returns a `shareUrl` that draws the same thing on the site, and answers a request it can't calculate, such as a solar return without a birth time, with HTTP 400 and an `error` saying what to change.

`GET /api/v1/places?q=` searches the same GeoNames cities as the page, most populous first, to find a birthplace's `latitude`, `longitude` and `timeZone`. Text after a comma narrows by region or country, e.g. `q=london, canada`. An optional `limit` of 1 to 25 defaults to 8. It returns `{ next, previous, count, result }`; it isn't paginated, so `next` and `previous` are always null.

Birth details are personal. Send them only in the request body, as the API requires. The API never logs or stores them, and its responses aren't cached.

## Linking to a birth chart

A link can fill in the form and draw a chart as soon as the page opens. The birth details go in the URL's `#` fragment, so browsers never send them to the server:

```
https://aster.myles.garden/#date=1990-05-15&time=14:30&place=6167865&house=placidus
```

That link draws a chart for 15 May 1990 at 2:30 pm in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, with Placidus houses.

| Parameter | Required | Format | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | Yes | `YYYY-MM-DD` | Birth date, e.g. `1990-05-15`. |
| `time` | Yes | `HH:MM`, 24-hour, or `unknown` | Local clock time at the birthplace, e.g. `14:30`. Aster works out the historical time zone and daylight saving offset itself; do not convert to UTC. Use `unknown` when the birth time isn't known. |
| `place` | Yes | GeoNames ID | A number identifying the birthplace, e.g. `6167865` for Toronto. See below. |
| `house` | No | House system | One of `placidus`, `koch`, `wholeSign`, `equal`, `porphyry`, `regiomontanus` or `campanus`. Defaults to `placidus`. |
| `aspects` | No | `major` or `all` | `all` adds the minor aspects: semi-sextile, semi-square, sesquiquadrate and quincunx. Defaults to `major`. |
| `orbs` | No | `tight`, `standard` or `wide` | Scales every aspect's orb: tight is three quarters of standard, wide a quarter more. Defaults to `standard`. |
| `ayanamsa` | No | Ayanamsa | Draws the chart in the sidereal zodiac, by one of `lahiri`, `faganBradley`, `krishnamurti`, `raman`, `yukteshwar` or `trueChitra`. Leave it out for the tropical zodiac, the default. Every position, cusp and angle moves back by the ayanamsa; whole sign houses start on the sidereal sign of the ascendant. Comparisons, transits, progressions and returns follow the chart's zodiac. |

If a parameter is missing or malformed, or the place isn't in Aster's index, the page shows an error instead of a chart.

### Unknown birth time

With `time=unknown`, Aster casts the chart for local noon and leaves out the houses, ascendant and midheaven, which depend on the exact time. The `house` parameter is then ignored. A body that changes sign during the birth date, most often the Moon, is shown with the other sign it may be in, e.g. "29° 40′ Cancer (may be Leo)":

```
https://aster.myles.garden/#date=1990-05-15&time=unknown&place=6167865
```

### Comparing two charts

Add a second person with `date2`, `time2` and `place2`, in the same formats as `date`, `time` and `place`. The page then draws a comparison: a bi-wheel with the first chart inside and the second outside, the aspects between the two charts, and where each person's planets fall in the other's houses. Both charts use `house`, `aspects` and `orbs`.

```
https://aster.myles.garden/#date=1990-05-15&time=14:30&place=6167865&house=placidus&date2=1988-11-02&time2=unknown&place2=2643743
```

That link compares someone born in Toronto at 2:30 pm on 15 May 1990 with someone born in London on 2 November 1988 at an unknown time.

Add `comparison=composite` to show a composite chart instead of the bi-wheel: one chart for the pair, with each body at the midpoint of the two people's positions, and houses cast around the midpoint of their midheavens at the latitude halfway between their birthplaces. It has houses only when both birth times are known.

### Transits

Add `transits` with a moment in UTC, to the minute, as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ`. The page then shows that moment's sky against the chart: a bi-wheel with the natal chart inside and the planets at that moment outside, the aspects they make to the natal planets within 2° of exact (or less, for a tighter orb), and which natal house each is in. A link can carry only one of `transits`, `progressed`, a second chart, `return` or `lunarReturn`.

```
https://aster.myles.garden/#date=1990-05-15&time=14:30&place=6167865&house=placidus&transits=2026-11-13T20:05Z
```

### Progressions

Add `progressed` with a date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, to show secondary progressions to that date: the chart moved on a day for each year of life. The page shows a bi-wheel with the natal chart inside and the progressed planets outside, the aspects they make to the natal planets within 1° of exact, and which natal house each is in. The date can't be before the birth.

```
https://aster.myles.garden/#date=1990-05-15&time=14:30&place=6167865&house=placidus&progressed=2026-11-14
```

### Solar returns

Add `return` with a year to show that year's solar return: the chart for the moment the Sun gets back to its natal position, near the birthday. It's cast at the birthplace unless the link gives another place, as `place_return`, or `lat_return`, `lon_return`, `tz_return` and optionally `name_return`, in the same formats as `place`, `lat`, `lon`, `tz` and `name`. A solar return needs the birth time.

```
https://aster.myles.garden/#date=1990-05-15&time=14:30&place=6167865&house=placidus&return=2026&place_return=2643743
```

That link shows the 2026 solar return for someone born in Toronto, cast in London.

### Lunar returns

Add `lunarReturn` with a date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, to show the lunar return in effect on that date: the chart for the latest moment the Moon got back to its natal position before that day ended, where it's cast. That happens about every 27 days, so giving the day a return comes on shows that return. It's cast at the birthplace unless the link gives another place, with the same `place_return`, or `lat_return`, `lon_return`, `tz_return` and `name_return`, as a solar return. A lunar return needs the birth time, and the date must be after the first return, about four weeks after birth.

```
https://aster.myles.garden/#date=1990-05-15&time=14:30&place=6167865&house=placidus&lunarReturn=2026-12-03
```

For either kind of return, add `returnStyle=biWheel` to set it against the natal chart: a bi-wheel with the natal chart inside and the return's planets outside, the aspects between them, and the natal house each return planet is in.

## Finding a place's GeoNames ID

Aster knows the cities in GeoNames' `cities15000` list: places with a population over 15,000. For a smaller town, give its coordinates instead (see below).

- Search https://www.geonames.org/ for the place. The ID is the number in the place's URL, e.g. `https://www.geonames.org/6167865/toronto.html`.
- Or search Aster's own index with `GET /api/v1/places?q=`, which returns each place's `id`.
- Or read the index whole, https://aster.myles.garden/data/places-all.json, most populous first. Each entry in `places` is `[name, asciiName, region, country, latitude, longitude, timeZoneIndex, geonameId]`, so the GeoNames ID is the last item. https://aster.myles.garden/data/places-top.json holds only the cities of 100,000 or more, in the same layout.

Some common IDs:

| Place | GeoNames ID |
| --- | --- |
| London, England, United Kingdom | 2643743 |
| Toronto, Ontario, Canada | 6167865 |
| London, Ontario, Canada | 6058560 |
| Montréal, Quebec, Canada | 6077243 |

## Places that aren't listed

Instead of `place`, give `lat` and `lon` in decimal degrees (south and west negative), `tz` as an IANA time zone, and optionally `name`. Use `lat2`, `lon2`, `tz2` and `name2` for a comparison's second person.

```
https://aster.myles.garden/#date=1990-05-15&time=14:30&lat=43.6833&lon=-79.7667&tz=America/Toronto&name=Brampton
```

## What the chart shows

- A chart wheel with the ascendant (or 0° Aries, without a birth time) at nine o'clock, zodiac signs coloured by element, house cusps, the four angles (AC, DC, MC, IC) and aspect lines.
- A Positions table: each body's sign, degree, retrograde status and house, plus the Ascendant and Midheaven. Without a birth time, houses and angles are left out.
- An Aspects table: each aspect between two bodies, with its orb. Major aspects by default; minor ones too when chosen, drawn as dashed lines on the wheel.
- Downloads of the wheel as SVG or PNG and of both tables as CSV, and a Copy link button that produces a link in the format above.
- In a comparison: the bi-wheel, an Aspects between you table, and each person's positions with a column for the house it falls in on the other person's chart.
- In a composite: one wheel, with the composite's positions and aspects.
- In a solar return: the return's wheel, positions and aspects, and the moment the Sun returns, on the clock where it's cast.
- In a lunar return: the same, for the moment the Moon returns.
- With transits: the bi-wheel, a Transits to your chart table, and the transiting planets' positions with the natal house each is in. Each transit has the moments it's exact (more than one when the planet turns retrograde, or none if it turns back first) and when it comes into and leaves orb, on the visitor's clock. The CSV download gives these in UTC.
- With progressions: the bi-wheel, a Progressions to your chart table, and the progressed planets' positions with the natal house each is in.
